full_judgment:
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of the instant civil petition for leave to appeal, are that the respondent Nos.1 to 3 herein as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.401 of 1986 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Satkhira, for declaration of title and confirmation of possession. The plaintiffs stated, inter alia, that 1.78 acres of land situated in 3 plots being Nos.1135, 1136 and 1137 appertaining to C.S. khatian No.1118/8 under Mouza Magura Gopinathpur, Police Station and District-Satkhira was broadly the subject matter of the suit wherein 54 decimals of land in plot No.1136 is in dispute. The jote belonged to Digambar Dhali and he had his homestead on the land and the C.S. record was correctly prepared. In course of time Digambar Dhali permitted Bagan Mandal his father's brother's son to reside in a portion of the suit land and thus Bagan Mandal continued to live there. But before publication of the C.S. record in the area Digambar Mandal had settled 3 bighas of land by way of registered pattan dated 23.04.1923 in favour of Ali Mohammad, the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners. Since the C.S parcha was not published by the time, no plot or khatian number could be mentioned in the said pattan. At the demise of Digambar Dhali his father's brother's son Bagan Mandal survived as his only heir and Bagan Mandal too died later leaving behind 2 sons, namely Madar Mandal and Swarup Mandal while in possession of the disputed plot No.1136 as their homestead. Madar Mandal and Swamp Mandal also with the passage of time died leaving these plaintiffs-respondent Nos.1-3 herein as their heirs. Subsequently, the plaintiffs came to know that the S.A. record in respect of the suit plot was prepared in khatian No.1072 in the name of Dabiruddin and thus the cause of action was triggered on 02.11.1986 when the defendants posed a threat to their possession on the basis of the alleged unfounded S.A. Parcha. Hence, the plaintiffs filed the suit. 

 3. The defendant-petitioners herein contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint. They contended, inter alia, that the entire jote of 1.78 acres of land which was subsequently recorded in C.S. khatian No.1118/08 used to be known as 3 bighas block and was owned by Digambar Dhali. Digambar Dhali by way of registered pattan dated 23.04.1923 settled the entire three bighas of land with Ali Mohammad, the pre-predecessor of the defendants. The defendants in their written statement have given a detailed description of sequential transfers and succession from Ali Mohammad. Hence, they prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 5. Mr. Md. Zakir Hossain, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that the Courts below erred in law in not considering at all the evidentiary value of the rent receipts exhibit-Ta(Series) showing payment of rent of the suit holding including the suit land since 1942 by Dabiruddin, defendant No.1 and arrived at a wrong decision to decide the suit in favour of the plaintiffs. He further submitted that the Courts below erred in law in not considering the conduct of the parties during the last 60 years, evidenced by S.A. Khatian and 7 registered deeds of transfer marked as exhibits-'Ga', 'Gha', 'Cha', 'Chha' and 'Ja' and arrived at an erroneous decision to give the verdict in favour of the plaintiffs. He submitted that the judgements of all the Courts below are bad in law and erroneous for not reading the pattan dated 23.04.1923 exhibit-2 in its entirety and a proper and complete reading of the same would justify interference by this Court. He submitted that the Courts below have misread the C.S. map and erroneously rejected the local investigation report exhibit-'Tha'. He submitted that the Courts below erred in law in holding that the plaintiffs are heirs of Digambar Dhali.
